name: Lutetium Lu-177 vipivotide tetraxetan
route: Intravenous injection every 6 weeks, up to 6 doses
status: FDA-approved (2022) for PSMA-positive metastatic prostate cancer; label widened in July 2026 to hormone-sensitive disease
mechanism: Radioactive lutetium-177 attached to a PSMA-binding molecule, delivering radiation directly to prostate cancer cells and their neighbors
uses: PSMA-positive hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, with ARPI

article.summary: Pluvicto (lutetium Lu-177 vipivotide tetraxetan) delivers radiation to PSMA-positive prostate cancer cells. It extended survival in advanced disease and is now approved for earlier-stage disease too.
article.takeaway: Pluvicto pairs radioactive lutetium-177 with a small molecule that sticks to PSMA, a protein expressed in prostate cancer. In the VISION trial of men with advanced castration-resistant disease, adding it to standard care extended median overall survival from 11.3 to 15.3 months.[^1] Later trials moved it earlier, and the August 2026 label covers PSMA-positive metastatic prostate cancer both before and after it stops responding to hormone-pathway drugs.[^2] Common problems are dry mouth, fatigue, nausea and low blood counts, and radiation-safety precautions apply.[^2]
glance: PSMA-positive metastatic prostate cancer, resistant or sensitive to hormone therapy
Intravenous injection every 6 weeks for up to 6 doses[^2]

blocks.text: PSMA (prostate-specific membrane antigen) is a protein on the surface of prostate cancer cells. A PET scan with a PSMA tracer shows whether a man's tumors express enough of it, and the label requires patients to be selected that way.[^2]

Pluvicto links lutetium-177, a radioactive atom that emits beta radiation, to a small peptide-like molecule that binds PSMA. Once attached, the radiation reaches the PSMA-expressing cells and nearby cells and damages their DNA.[^2]

items: **Earlier disease:** with androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) therapy, for adults with PSMA-positive metastatic prostate cancer not yet treated with, or still responding to, androgen pathway drugs[^2]
**Resistant disease:** for adults with PSMA-positive metastatic cancer that has stopped responding, after ARPI treatment, when taxane chemotherapy can be delayed or has already been given[^2]

rows: 831 men with advanced PSMA-positive castration-resistant cancer
Median survival 15.3 vs 11.3 months (hazard ratio 0.62); progression-free survival 8.7 vs 3.4 months[^1]
468 taxane-naive men whose cancer progressed on an ARPI
Progression-free survival 9.3 vs 5.6 months against switching ARPI (hazard ratio 0.41)[^3]
28% lower risk of progression or death when added to hormone therapy plus an ARPI (hazard ratio 0.72)[^4]

blocks.text: In PSMAfore, 57% of men assigned to switch ARPI later crossed over to Pluvicto.[^3] In PSMAddition, median progression-free survival had not been reached in either arm at the interim analysis.[^4]

The label dose is 7.4 GBq (200 mCi) by intravenous injection every 6 weeks for up to 6 doses, or until the cancer progresses or side effects become unacceptable. Doses can be paused, reduced or stopped for toxicity. After each dose, patients follow radiation-safety steps: limit close contact with others for 2 days (7 days with children and pregnant women), refrain from sex for 7 days, drink extra fluids and urinate often.[^2]

items: **Most common (20% or more):** low lymphocyte, hemoglobin, neutrophil and platelet counts, fatigue, dry mouth, nausea, lower kidney filtration, and changes in liver enzymes and electrolytes[^2]
**Myelosuppression:** can be severe or life-threatening, so blood counts are checked[^2]
**Kidney toxicity:** kidney function is monitored and patients stay well hydrated[^2]

**Radiation and fertility:** adds to cumulative radiation exposure, may cause temporary or permanent infertility, and can harm a fetus, so men with partners who could become pregnant should use effective contraception[^2]

blocks.text: Serious (grade 3 or higher) adverse events were more frequent than with control in VISION (52.7% vs 38.0%) and PSMAddition (51% vs 43%), but less frequent than with ARPI switching in PSMAfore (36% vs 48%).[^1][^4][^3] Dry mouth occurred in 46% in PSMAddition.[^4]

evidence.label: Strong: three large randomized phase 3 trials
evidence.text: VISION showed a survival gain in advanced disease.[^1] PSMAfore and PSMAddition showed longer time without radiographic progression in earlier settings, with survival data still maturing.[^3][^4]

faq.a: Men whose tumors show enough PSMA on a PET scan; the label requires selection with an approved PSMA PET product.[^2]

It is a radioligand: a radioactive atom attached to a small, peptide-like molecule that targets PSMA. It is a different kind of agent from hormone peptides such as [leuprolide](/peptides/leuprolide), which lower testosterone.
In VISION it did, in advanced castration-resistant disease (15.3 vs 11.3 months).[^1] In earlier settings the main result so far is longer time without radiographic progression.[^3][^4]
